description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to expand long-term finance to private firms in selected infrastructure sectors in Eastern and Southern Africa

The objective of the Eastern and Southern African Trade and Development Bank, and Common Market - Regional Infrastructure Finance Facility Project for Eastern and Southern Africa is to expand long-term finance to private firms in selected infrastructure sectors in Eastern and Southern Africa. The Project has three components. 1. Project and Infrastructure Finance Facility component will provide long-term finance to project finance and infrastructure sub-projects that meet development impact criteria. Sub-projects will be selected using a two-stage approach: Stage 1: Mandatory eligibility criteria: All sub-projects will be located in International Development Association (IDA)-eligible countries in Eastern and Southern Africa and will have to show commercial bankability, leveraging of private finance, compliance with the Environmental and Social (E and S) List of Excluded Activities, and with the IDA sustainable development finance policy as applicable to the respective countries; Stage 2: Prioritization criteria: All eligible sub-projects will be scored against objective, measurable and verifiable criteria along four dimensions: (i) Project benefits and contribution to corporate commitments including job creation, emissions reduction, low income targeting, gender actions; (ii) Levels of economic and financial returns; (iii) Strategic relevance with the expansion to Fragility, Conflict, and Violence (FCV) countries, and cross-border benefits in terms of trade and investment flows or transfers of technology; (iv) Technical readiness. 2. COVID-19 Infrastructure Sector Small and Medium-sized Enterprise (SME) Facility component will facilitate access to debt financing to SMEs, primarily targeting renewable energy SMEs such as solar home-systems (SHS), and also SMEs in the infrastructure value chain operating in Southern and Eastern Africa. In the COVID-19 context, this component will preserve household economic activity in the short-term and support firm productivity in the medium-term. 3. Technical Assistance component has two subcomponents. 3a. Capacity Building and Technical Assistance to Eastern and Southern African Trade and Development Bank (TDB) subcomponent will provide the needed expertise to support TDB's strategic decision to scale-up project and infrastructure finance and strengthen its capacity on E and S. 3b. Capacity Building and Technical Assistance to Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Secretariat subcomponent will support the enabling environment for private infrastructure finance with a focus on building a regional off-grid energy market.

condition.narrative: COMESA Financing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.A: The Recipient shall, by no later than 3 months after the Effective Date: (i)appoint, from among its senior staff, a Project coordinator; (ii) appoint from among its staff, or recruit, a procurementspecialist and a financial management specialist; all for the Project Team, and in each case with qualifications, experience andterms of reference acceptable to the Association.

TDB Financing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.E: The Recipient shall prepare a report, in form and substance acceptable to theAssociation, setting forth its pipeline of proposed Infrastructure Sub-Credits for each six (6) month period of Projectimplementation. The Recipient shall promptly furnish such report to the Association as part of the Project Reports (provided thatthe first such report shall be furnished to the Association by no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date), afford theAssociation a reasonable opportunity to exchange views with the Recipient on such report, and thereafter proceed with itsconsideration of the financing of such Infrastructure Sub-Credits taking into account the Association's views.

comment.narrative:
PFM achieved 114% of target and PCM ratio achieved is 4.05:1. As a result of PCM complementing financing from TDB and other DFIs, off-grid renewable energy companies revenues have increased to USD 60M. The expanded deployment of solar products has contributed to broadening the government tax base, resulting in USD 8M in additional public revenue. It is estimated that approx. 350,000 people have been able to spend more time in productive economic activities due to improved access to off-grid renewable energy solutions.
This indicator measures the total private sector finance (debt and equity) mobilized from project sponsors, including DFIs, for sub-projects financed under RIFF. The reported figure excludes the IDA credit line. The target is based on an assumed private capital mobilization ratio of 3:1 relative to Component One financing.
While this indicator includes DFI funding mobilized through TDB, PCM per 2018 reference guide of MDB, does not include DFI funding.

title.narrative: Number of staff trained in COMESA Secretariat, member countries and market participants on off-grid, PPP and E&S

comment.narrative:
138% of target achieved. Key trainings and TA were conducted on PPP project identification and capacity building, TDB infrastructure finance and risk management, and the VeraSol QA Framework, as well as broader capacity building for contracting authorities, among others.
Renewable energy–specific trainings and TA carried out included off-grid renewable energy market needs assessments, enhancement of energy regulatory capacity, and support for frameworks to enforce standards for renewable energy technologies, among others.
These trainings covered Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff, the COMESA Secretariat, TDB staff, country ministry officials, contracting authorities, as well as other relevant entities and market participants.
This indicator measures the cumulative number of staff trained from the COMESA Secretariat, member countries, and market participants who received training on off-grid energy, public–private partnerships (PPPs), and environmental and social (E&S) aspects.

title.narrative: Number of private firms financed across Eastern and Southern Africa

comment.narrative:
23% of target achieved. As the number of private firms financed has reached six, it is estimated that approximately 350,000 people are using solar products to support business and income-generating activities. The reported results reflect sub-projects supporting off-grid renewable energy.
This indicator tracks the number of firms receiving direct financing under RIFF across Eastern and Southern Africa. It captures only direct sub-borrowers and excludes firms that benefit indirectly from RIFF support, such as contractors or suppliers.

title.narrative: Average maturity of TDB's Project and Infrastructure Finance Portfolio

comment.narrative:
106% of target achieved. The average maturity of the TDB portfolio has increased significantly, more than doubling from five years to 11.7 years. As a result, it is estimated that approximately 660,000 people are undertaking increased economic activities.
This indicator is measured at the global portfolio level for Component One and reflects a weighted average maturity. While Component One transactions typically have longer tenors, Component Two transactions are, by design, associated with shorter maturities. As Component One continues to disburse, the overall portfolio maturity is expected to increase further.

title.narrative: People provided with new or improved electricity service

comment.narrative:
202% of target achieved. Over 260,000 households, representing more than three million individuals, have gained access to electricity. On average, households have extended their daily lighting use by 3.95 hours. In some cases, customers use solar home systems (SHS) to stabilize electricity supply where grid service is unreliable.
These results reflect the number of people gaining access to off-grid energy through SME off-grid transactions approved by TDB. The figures capture increased access over the medium term.

title.narrative: Number of COMESA policies and guidelines including guidance on the off-grid energy sector

comment.narrative:
120% of target achieved. Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) policies and guidelines now include several instruments relevant to the off-grid energy sector. These include the Model Solar Standards, approved by the COMESA Ministers of Infrastructure on 14 September 2023; the Model Energy Policy, also approved by the Ministers of Infrastructure on 14 September 2023; and the Model Customs Common Tariffs, which are pending approval by the COMESA Ministers of Trade. Additional instruments include the Model PPP Framework, the Mini-Grid Tariff-Setting Methodology and Tool, and the Solar Product Registration System.
This indicator measures the number of COMESA policies and guidelines that include guidance on the off-grid energy sector.

title.narrative: Regional Quality Assurance Standards for off-grid energy products

comment.narrative:
The COMESA Model Solar Standards were approved by the COMESA Ministers of Infrastructure at their meeting held on 14 September 2023 in Kigali, Rwanda. Following approval, technical assistance was provided to selected Member States—Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Malawi, South Sudan, and Zimbabwe—by the end of 2023.
This indicator measures the preparation and adoption of a regional Quality Assurance (QA) framework for off-grid energy products by COMESA.

title.narrative: Citizens reached through the consumer education and citizen engagement program satisfied with the program

comment.narrative:
The RIFF PIU engaged member state citizens and stakeholders through ministries, agencies, and institutions, including energy ministries and regulators, power utilities, rural electrification agencies, customs and standards authorities, ministries of trade and finance, academia, renewable energy associations, mini-grid developers and consumers, as well as the Africa Mini-Grid Developers Association (AMDA), Africa Union for Renewable Energy (AFUR), and the Trade and Development Bank (TDB).
The RIFF PIU also reached private sector companies through AMDA, with whom COMESA has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
Outreach was conducted through RIFF workshops, media briefings, and branded materials, supported by a Visibility and Advocacy Strategy including media engagement workshops, a promotional video, and the RIFF website.
This indicator measures the percentage of citizens reached through the consumer education and engagement program reporting “satisfied” or “very satisfied.”
